description: This plot illustrates the relationship between the Co-occurrence Number and ACC (%) for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and employs a logarithmic scale for values above zero, with major tick marks labeled at 0, $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. The plotted data points are located at approximate x-values of 3, 30, 300, and 3000. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and uses a linear scale ranging from 60 to 85, with tick marks at regular intervals of 5 units (60, 65, 70, 75, 80). The "Base" line is a solid black line with circle markers, showing a steady increase from approximately 63.8% at the first x-value to 71.0% at the final x-value. The "FT" line is a solid blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, increasing steadily from roughly 65.2% to 73.0%. The "IKE" line is a solid red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, rising from about 67.4% to 75.2%. The "MEND" line is a solid brown line with diamond markers, showing an upward trend from approximately 70.7% to 80.1%. The "MEMIT" line is a solid purple line with pentagon markers, increasing from roughly 69.5% to 77.5%. Finally, the "ROME" line is a solid green line with square markers, which rises steadily from about 74.3% at the start of the x-axis to 83.8% at the end.
